scope: At most eight existing submitted deliverables: four Gemini solver outputs and four matched GPT-6.1 Sol outputs, judged independently by Claude Sonnet.
selection_timing: Primary outputs and some judge-pilot outputs were already observed; freeze this task/model pairing before the secondary judge results. This is an exploratory amendment, not a preregistration before the primary study.

candidate_policy.google/gemini-4-argon: The exact first-pass supplemental run only; no second repeat or replacement if it fails.
candidate_policy.openai/gpt-6.1-sol: Submitted original primary first; otherwise the earliest completed submitted recovery or explicitly recorded adapter_repair of this same task. Freeze the exact selected run before secondary judging; never substitute by judge verdict.

request_policy: Use unchanged native source/artifact evidence preparation, frozen task rubric, strict validator, all output render batches, max_tokens 8000 and medium reasoning from the primary grading runner. Only judge model changes. Existing judgments, including invalid responses, are never retried.

budget.request_count_note: Output-image batching can require more than one request per deliverable; report actual physical requests and cost. Keep missing or budget-stopped cells visible.

interpretation: The original Gemini judge is cross-family for OpenAI and Anthropic solvers but self-family for the Gemini solver. Keep that structural difference visible per row.
Sonnet provides a common cross-family judge for the matched Gemini and Sol deliverables. Do not use Sonnet's own outputs in this secondary comparison.
Different verdicts can reflect judge error, solver quality or incomplete evidence; self-family status is not evidence of self-preference.
Compare the same artifact under both judges separately from comparing different solver artifacts under the same judge.
Primary, recovery and adapter-repair artifacts retain distinct provenance. Repairs and extra attempts prevent a clean first-pass solver ranking.
Do not pool self-family and cross-family verdicts into an overall model ranking or acceptance rate. Human acceptance and judge accuracy remain unmeasured for these new outputs.
Report task-level statuses and valid-pair denominators, retaining invalid, missing and uncertain judgments outside binary agreement denominators.
